conditions.title: none
conditions.body: Problem statement plus the repo with AGENTS.md removed. A straw-man lower bound — not the real baseline.

conditions.title: agents_md
conditions.body: Repo as maintainers shipped it, including their hand-written AGENTS.md. This is the real baseline: most candidate repos already document agent instructions in-tree.

conditions.title: agents_md+memory
conditions.body: Maintainer AGENTS.md plus lessons transferred from train tasks. The question is whether learned memory beats what maintainers wrote by hand.

agents_md_coverage.note: LangGraph's AGENTS.md is silent on DeltaChannel invariants.

transfer_pairs.label: Chain C
transfer_pairs.summary: Fresh-thread snapshot through bulk task ids

transfer_pairs.label: Control
transfer_pairs.summary: Unrelated task run with Pair A lessons loaded — contamination check

pipeline.title: Parent commit
pipeline.body: Historical parent of the fix — the buggy tree.

pipeline.title: git archive
pipeline.body: Materialize the tree with no .git — no answer in history.

pipeline.title: Overlay tests
pipeline.body: Copy only the fix’s test files onto the parent tree.

pipeline.title: Gate: confirm they fail
pipeline.body: Control run: parent must fail the overlaid tests before any agent starts.

pipeline.title: Agent attempts
pipeline.body: Same agent, one memory condition, budgeted tool loop.

pipeline.title: Re-run and diff
pipeline.body: Score with the same tests; compare per-test outcomes and capture the patch.

premise: Accumulating context is not the same as learning. Longer prompts and retrieved snippets can look like memory while the model still fails the same class of bug.
BrainDiff holds the coding agent constant and varies only what it is allowed to remember — then scores with the repository’s own tests, not an LLM judge.

hero.question: Does agent memory actually help?
supporting: Same agent. Real historical LangGraph bugs. Three memory conditions.
Scored by the repo’s tests — no LLM judges in the loop.

limits.title: Floor effect
limits.body: Subtle fixes (roughly 63 to a few hundred source lines) may leave the baseline at zero without proving memory is useless — a scored failure is still the honest start.

limits.title: One repo, n=9
limits.body: All tasks are DeltaChannel / update_state bugs in langchain-ai/langgraph. Transfer claims do not generalize past this pool yet.

limits.title: Lesson contamination
limits.body: Whether a transferred lesson leaks the answer is audited by hand (plus the unrelated-task control), not by an automated judge.

limits.title: Partial credit
limits.body: Partial is a per-test proxy against the parent’s failures — not a proof of correctness.
